A factor connects a pattern across samples to a pattern across features.
Start with a model fitted directly by flashier; no special fitting wrapper is required.

## Fit and extract

GTEx association z-scores are bundled with flashier. Rows are SNP–gene pairs;
columns are tissues. These tissues do not supply donor-level replication.

```{r fit}
library(flashier.utils)
data("gtex", package = "flashier")
set.seed(1)
fit <- flashier::flash(gtex, greedy_Kmax = 3, backfit = TRUE, verbose = 0)
view <- standardize_factors(fit, sample_side = "columns",
                            feature_scale = "association_z_score")
activity <- factor_activity(view)  # samples × factors
effects <- factor_effects(view)    # features × the same factors
```

Use uniquely named rows and columns. Declare `sample_side = "rows"` when
samples occupy rows. Preprocess before fitting; `feature_scale` records units
and does not transform data. Unnamed existing fits are rejected rather than
assigned potentially misleading identities.

## Interpret one factor

```{r features}
factor_features(view, factor = "F1", select = "largest", n = 5)[,
  c("feature", "estimate")]
```

Effects retain their sign. A factor's sign can reverse on both sides without
changing reconstruction; it does not by itself mean activation or repression.
Use `select = "distinctive"` to rank separation from competing programs.

```{r activity, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
plot_factor_activity(view)
```

The heatmap shows tissue activity in the declared coordinates. For your own
matrix, use metadata summaries before assigning biological labels.
